basis: Erythroid leukemia is a neoplasm of blood-forming cells and bone marrow.
Carcinoma originates in tonsillar oropharyngeal mucosa; pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis. Referred ear pain does not indicate ear damage.
Optic nerve/visual pathway glioma; the name specifies the ocular optic nerve, while the definition and synonyms include intracranial optic tracts.
Defining immune dysfunction, neurodevelopmental defects and colitis; dermatitis 2/2. Cap excludes retinal/hepatic disease (1/2 each) and reduced bone density (1/1).
Carcinoma originates in the lung; metastatic sites are not defining involvement across this umbrella.
Exogenous glucocorticoid excess defines this endocrine syndrome; additional organ damage is not established independently of treatment effects.
Abnormal curvature of ocular refractive surfaces impairs focusing and vision.
Lysosomal lipid storage with defining liver injury; splenomegaly 2/2 with reported hypersplenism/cytopenias supports splenic dysfunction. Atherosclerosis is separately diagnosed.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the disorder; visual and cardiac abnormalities are described as less frequent.
Defining skeletal/dental defects; microcephaly/tremor 2/2 and hypomyelination 1/2; cardiac defects 1/2. Cap excludes subcutaneous fat loss (1/2).
Immune-mediated epidermal necrosis; destructive oral mucositis occurs in roughly 90%, and ocular surface epithelial injury in about 50-80%.
CRYGC-related cataract directly affects the ocular lens and vision.
Epilepsy with an explicitly immune-mediated etiology and central nervous system inflammation.
Renal failure/nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy define the syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 3/8 (38%). Hepatic fibrosis 2/8 is below threshold.
Disease of cardiac muscle; myocardial involvement does not establish skeletal muscle disease.
Benign smooth muscle neoplasm originating in the colon; visceral smooth muscle is assigned to its organ of origin.
ACTA1-related skeletal muscle disease. Respiratory dysfunction reflects respiratory muscle weakness; cardiac involvement is explicitly rare.
Destructive bone remodeling; hearing loss is characteristic, dental defects occur in 80-99%, optic atrophy in 30-79%. Hypertension is separately diagnosed.
Follicular occlusion causes destructive scalp inflammation and scarring alopecia; associated infections are secondary rather than the defining disease mechanism.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes; hearing loss occurs in roughly 50% of MELAS, but MTTQ-specific frequency is uncertain.
Primary breast carcinoma lies outside the axes; hormone receptor expression does not make it an endocrine gland disease.
Congenital dysferlin-related skeletal muscle disease causes hypotonia and weakness; motor delay reflects myopathy rather than demonstrated CNS disease.
Defining skeletal abnormalities, intellectual disability and cardiac anomalies; strabismus and ptosis each occur in 30-79%, supporting ocular dysfunction.
Urinary tract obstruction directly damages the kidneys and impairs renal function.
Inherited factor IX coagulation deficiency causes abnormal bleeding; chronic joint damage is not established as common in this moderate subgroup.
